mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically for three consecutive weeks (-32.3 to -21.9). This autocorrelated recovery momentum is expected to persist, pushing the next 28-day mean above the last 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:three consecutive weekly increases in RETAIL_REC
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC reverses and falls for two or more consecutive weeks within the next 28 days despite prior three-week uptrend.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility crosses above -15 (approaching near-baseline), commuters resuming office routines generate incidental retail trips near transit hubs and office districts, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -15 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -25.9 to -13.9 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise or declines in the two weeks after WORKPLACES crosses -15, despite the threshold being met.

mechanism_narrative: Declining RESIDENTIAL time combined with rising TRANSIT usage jointly indicate households are substituting home-bound behavior for out-of-home mobility routed through transit, a precursor to increased retail visitation over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls while TRANSIT rises in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 16.4 to 10.6 while TRANSIT rose from -31.7 to -23.0 over same period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC 4-week mean does not increase even though RESIDENTIAL continues falling and TRANSIT continues rising jointly.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime where both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT show sustained multi-week gains, this reflects relaxed government restrictions on movement, which mechanically permits higher retail and recreation footfall over the following four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved every week over the snapshot window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stagnates or declines over the next 28 days despite continued simultaneous improvement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT, indicating policy relaxation is not translating to retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has plateaued and slightly declined (-27.4 to -29.3) after an initial recovery, suggesting outdoor recreational substitution is saturating; as weather/seasonal appeal of parks wanes, displaced recreation demand shifts toward indoor retail and recreation venues within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS fails to improve week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -27.4 to -29.0 to -29.3 over last three weeks, showing stagnation/decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks of PARKS stagnating, or both PARKS and RETAIL_REC decline together.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has plateaued near +11 to +13, indicating essential-goods demand has saturated; once this ceiling is reached, any further increase in overall out-of-home activity will flow disproportionately into discretionary retail and recreation trips rather than grocery trips, raising RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM week-on-week change falls below 1.5 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM changed only 12.0 to 12.7 to 11.6 over last three weeks, a plateau
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following GROCERY_PHARM plateau, or GROCERY_PHARM resumes strong growth while RETAIL_REC stalls.

mechanism_narrative: The steady week-on-week decline in RESIDENTIAL time (16.4 to 10.6) directly signals reduced home-confinement behavior; this behavioral shift mechanically frees time for out-of-home discretionary activity, raising RETAIL_REC within a single week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined every week over the snapshot period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week immediately following a continued decline in RESIDENTIAL.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both jump by more than 5 points week-on-week simultaneously, this co-movement signals an official policy announcement loosening capacity or distancing restrictions, which within four weeks compounds into a larger-than-trend rise in RETAIL_REC as the policy relaxation generalizes across sectors.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise more than 5 points week-on-week in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose 4.8 points and WORKPLACES rose 6.3 points between t-3w and t-2w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC 4-week mean does not exceed the prior 4-week mean despite a joint TRANSIT-WORKPLACES surge exceeding the 5-point threshold.
